name: CCM
summary: CCM is located at the LANSCE Lujan Center, Los Alamos National Laboratory, New Mexico. It is a series of liquid-argon experiments for beam-produced light dark matter and sterile neutrinos.
detection_principle: An 800 MeV pulsed proton beam strikes a target to produce dark-matter candidates. Liquid argon records recoils or electromagnetic energy; arrival time relative to the beam and shielding suppress neutron/neutrino backgrounds.

key_parameters.value: Approximately 10 tonnes, about 20 m from the neutron/neutrino source

key_parameters.name: CCM200 readout
key_parameters.value: 200 eight-inch PMTs; the 2025 technical paper uses a 7-tonne fiducial volume

key_parameters.name: Beam
key_parameters.value: 800 MeV protons; pulse structure discriminates backgrounds

results.summary: The 2019 CCM120 engineering sample constrains light dark matter and leptophobic models, without a discovery claim.
CCM200 achieved event-by-event Cherenkov-light identification for sub-MeV electron events; this is a detector-technology result, rather than a dark-matter discovery.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered.
